records.text: Gibbert is a weapon merchant. He repairs equipment and sells weapons to visitors.
Stegodons are among the dinosaur kinds found in Un'Goro Crater, where the Venomhide Hatchling's feeding quest names them as prey alongside diemetradons and pterrordaxes.
The Plated Stegodon is a named stegodon variety found in Un'Goro Crater. Its title distinguishes this form among the crater's named stegodons.
The Spiked Stegodon is a named stegodon variety found in Un'Goro Crater. Its title distinguishes this form among the crater's named stegodons.
The Thunderstomp Stegodon is a named stegodon variety found in Un'Goro Crater. Its title distinguishes this form among the crater's named stegodons.
Ravasaur is a raptor of Un'Goro Crater, where it is found across the zone. The species' females guard eggs and can attack when their nests are approached. In combat, this Ravasaur uses Rend.
Ravasaur Runner is one of the ravasaur creatures found across Un'Goro Crater.
Ravasaur Hunter is a raptor found in the western part of Un'Goro Crater. It uses Rend in combat.

Venomhide Ravasaur is a vicious animal whose toxin makes it unsafe to handle without immunity. Its young must be trained from hatching; an unhatched egg can be raised into a mount with Mor'vek's guidance. In combat, the Venomhide uses a venom ability.

Bloodpetal Lasher is one of the troublesome Bloodpetal plant pests in Un'Goro, alongside the Thresher, Flayer, and Trapper. Larion asks for Lashers to be hunted after blaming Muigin's pests for making their situation worse. The Lasher uses poison and Lash in combat.
A Bloodpetal Flayer is one of Muigin's plant pests in Un'Goro Crater, named among those Larion wants hunted. It attacks with poison and flaying vines.
A Bloodpetal Thresher is one of Muigin's plant pests in Un'Goro Crater, named among those Larion wants hunted.
A Bloodpetal Trapper is one of Muigin's plant pests in Un'Goro Crater, named among those Larion wants hunted.
Tar Beast is an elemental creature that casts Sticky Tar.
Tar Lurker is an elemental creature that uses Black Sludge in combat and casts Sticky Tar.
Tar Lord is an elemental creature that uses Entangling Roots in combat.
Scorching Elemental is an elemental combatant that uses Scorch.
Living Blaze is a fire-named elemental encountered as a combatant; it reacts when engaged.
Tar Creeper is an elemental creature that uses Trample in combat.
The Gorishi Wasp is an insect. In combat, it casts Silithid Pox.
The Gorishi Worker is an insect. Like the Gorishi Wasp, it casts Silithid Pox in combat.
The Gorishi Reaver is a creature whose combat behavior includes a Cleave attack.
The Gorishi Stinger is an insect. In combat, it casts Silithid Pox.
The Gorishi Tunneler is an insect. Its combat behavior includes an attack called Tunneler Acid.
When badly hurt, the Primal Ooze can begin copying itself; it can also summon a Gargantuan Ooze.
Stone Guardian is a stone creature.
The Ravasaur Matriarch is a solitary, exceptionally powerful ravasaur. Her combat behavior includes using Rend.
Clutchmother Zavas is a solitary, exceptionally powerful creature. She uses Cleave, Pierce Armor and Gorishi Egg in combat.
Gruff is a solitary, sturdy creature. His combat behavior includes Chained Bolt and Thunderclap.
King Mosh is a solitary, sturdy creature. His combat behavior includes a terrifying roar and a trample attack.
Uhk'loc is a formidable beast. In combat, he uses an uppercut and, after killing an opponent, casts Battle Shout.

Linken is an amnesiac traveler who recalls arriving in Un'Goro after a crash, but struggles to remember his name and past. He is piecing together why he came and what his sword means, with help from J.D. Collie, who was kind to him when he first arrived, and Donova Snowden, who can temper the blade. Linken eventually remembers that his journey was meant to end in a fight with Blazerunner; believing he is no longer the hero, he entrusts that task to the player and says the Golden Flame should be protected from evil.

Larion blames Muigin's shortcut for their being lost and refuses to speak again without an apology. Larion accuses Muigin of growing Bloodpetal pests to cause annoyance, preferring retaliation to reconciliation. Friend Marvon's workshop is sought for a gadget to fight back; Larion knows the zapper needs a Bloodpetal sprout to calibrate it.

Muigin admits a vengeful grudge against Larion, claiming to know the way out but refusing to leave until Larion admits fault. He hopes to train Bloodpetals to obey commands and uses Atal'ai haze on sprouts to get Larion's attention. Unsure of the plants' apparent intelligence and admitting limited expertise, he seeks help from friend Gregan Brewspewer.
Bloodpetal pests are plant-like nuisances.
A young diemetradon of Un'Goro Crater, it attacks with a ripping bite when drawn into a fight.
A diemetradon of Un'Goro Crater, it answers threats with a dire growl.
A fledgling pterrordax of Un'Goro Crater, it swoops at threats in combat.
A pterrordax of Un'Goro Crater, it uses a terrifying screech against threats.
A frenzied pterrordax of Un'Goro Crater, it is among the growing threat to travelers in the area; a wanted notice calls for reducing its numbers. In combat it can terrify its foes.

Williden Marshal leads Marshal Expeditions, a non-aligned band of scientists and explorers that includes his sister and their companions. In Un'Goro Crater, savage beasts drove the expedition from its camps, leaving vital food and research equipment behind; Williden also feared his journal was lost. He values the team's research and is deeply grateful for help recovering their supplies.

Hol'anyee Marshal is the chief scientist and biologist of Marshal Expeditions, which she travels with her brother and companions. Her work in Un'Goro Crater investigates the Gorishi insects, whose presence she considers alien to the local ecology. Despite the expedition's dangerous setback and near-stranded situation, she wants research to continue and studies samples from their hive walls.

Spark Nilminer is chief digger for Marshal Expeditions, but jokes that he dislikes digging. The expedition needs dinosaur bones for research by Wil and Hol, and Spark accepts bones from live stegodons or diemetradons as well as ancient ones. After the beasts nearly overwhelmed the group at Terror Run, he is anxious to escape Un'Goro and prefers not to know how the bones were obtained.
Petra Grossen is a questgiver in Un'Goro Crater.
Dadanga is a large herbivore in Un'Goro Crater. Quest text depicts her as hungry and describes her accepting sprouts and nudging a wrapped package toward the feeder.

Blazerunner is an aura-protected elemental guarding the Golden Flame at Fire Plume Ridge. He is described as dangerous, casts his aura and Blast Wave, and can lose the aura when hit by a specific spell.
The Gorishi Egg is a creature in Un'Goro Crater.
Parrot is a critter found at several locations in Un'Goro Crater.

Karna Remtravel is an engineer who hopes to discover things from lost cultures, following in his uncle Remtravel’s footsteps. He built A-Me 01, a mechanical ape with scrying-gem eyes, to blend in among the apes of Un’Goro Crater and let him see what she saw. After losing contact with her at Fungal Rock, he asks for help finding her. He is pleased when she returns, worries about her dents, and hopes to repair her so she can come home.

Torwa Pathfinder is a spiritually minded hunter who honors the Earth Mother and the spirits of the creatures he tracks. He sees hunting as a test of skill, spirit, and mind, and values courage over race or profession. He seeks to prove his own strength and help his tribe; the loss of his brother to Lar'korwi shapes his plan to provoke and confront the beast. He also regards U'cha as one of the Earth Mother's great sons and a formidable hunting challenge.
Torwa Pathfinder names U’cha as a huge ape among Un’Goro’s gorillas and one of the Earth Mother’s greatest sons. He presents the hunt for U’cha’s pelt as a test for a would-be great hunter.

A-Me 01 is a mechanical ape created by Karna Remtravel to blend in with Un'Goro's apes and observe them through her scrying-gem eyes. After losing power, she speaks in short, simple phrases about being good and finding her way home to Karna. Her repair involves replacing a burnt-out mithril casing and restarting her power.

Spraggle Frock is Ringo's friend and worries when Ringo stays away too long while exploring the volcano. He sends a canteen in case Ringo needs help on the way back. Spraggle is also frightened by the pterrordax around Marshal's Refuge and says their threat makes him wary of venturing out; he wants travelers in the area protected.

Shizzle is a stranded inventor in Marshal’s Refuge, building a flying machine whose wings he plans to make from local reptile scales. He says he is poor at finding his way and frightened of gryphons and wind riders, so he asks others to gather the materials; he expects the finished flyer to work and has already chosen the name “Pwned!”

Ringo is an explorer who became dangerously faint from the heat while exploring near Fire Plume Ridge. He asks for help reaching his friend Spraggle at Marshal’s Refuge and explains how Spraggle’s canteen can revive him if he passes out. His speech stays woozy and self-deprecating as he struggles onward, and he is relieved to make it back to Spraggle.

Krakle investigates the heat behind Un’Goro’s hot springs. He made a thermometer, humorously calibrated in “degrees Kraklenheit,” and asks others to take readings at Fire Plume Ridge because he is afraid of its fire elementals. The results suggest a link between the volcano’s temperature and the springs, though he says he still needs to check his equations. He points interested researchers toward his friend Donova Snowden in Winterspring to investigate springs far from volcanoes.
Gryfe is a flight master who offers flight-route information. He summons an enraged gryphon and wyvern when attacked.

Quixxil is jumpy and reacts with alarm when Umi's Mechanical Yeti chases him, pleading for it to be taken away. Afterward, he looks relieved; he says people insist on scaring him and vows to be ready next time.

Mor'vek trains riders for Un'Goro's venomous Venomhide ravasaurs. He insists that riders build toxin resistance before handling eggs, then raise and train a hatchling with careful attention from the start. He calls the process demanding, remarks that the eggs seem to be growing scarce, and teases a successful learner as stubborn as his wife.
Nergal is a General Goods merchant in Un'Goro Crater. He offers goods for browsing and also handles quest-related interaction, giving him both a shop and quest-giver role.
A blazing elemental invader that attacks with Blast Wave.

Baron Charr declares his aim to burn the Crater of its impurity, taunts its absent heroes, and warns that all will be consumed. He presents the invasion as purifying destruction and challenges the world's heroes to face him, while his fire attack makes him a direct threat to the Crater's defenders.

Simone the Inconspicuous greets visitors with sunny warmth, calling them friends and urging them to enjoy life. A visitor directly challenges this friendly presentation as a disguise and calls her a temptress, exposing the adversarial role beneath it.
Precious is Simone's pet. It gives a low growl followed by two barks.
Elder Thunderhorn is reflective, recalling a past when “we” lived by the hunt for glory and honor, then wondering whether life is so different now.

The Etymidian is a colossal stone weapon awakened by an Omega Rune. It asks whether it is needed, and says it has bound its being into the rune; it seeks passage to Freya's lands to help counter the blight of undeath in Sholazar Basin.

High Cultist Herenn angrily confronts the player for leading his side to the Etymidian, which he calls the only being able to stand against their armies. He declares they will never bring it back to Northrend.
A Death's Hand acolyte.
A young venomhide ravasaur found in Un'Goro Crater, this creature is identified as a raptor.

A venomhide hatchling that communicates its hunger by sketching prey in the dirt and making a biting motion. Its associated quests center on feeding it fresh meat, and its recorded activity text describes it tearing into and devouring food.
